# First, let's understand what C standard format codes look like by looking at Python docs
# and understanding the mapping needed for dt_format_to_regex
# Common C strftime codes -> regex patterns:
# %Y = 4-digit year, %m = month (01-12), %d = day (01-31)
# %H = hour (00-23), %M = minute (00-59), %S = second (00-59)
# %f = microseconds, %z = timezone offset, %a/%A = day name, %b/%B = month name
# %p = AM/PM, %c = locale date/time, %x = locale date, %X = locale time
# %j = day of year, %U/%W = week number, %w = weekday, %G/%V/%u = ISO year/week/day
# %n = newline, %t = tab, %% = literal %

# Let's also check if there are any existing references to dt_format_to_regex
import re
content = open('parse.py').read()
matches = re.findall(r'dt_format', content)
print("dt_format matches:", len(matches))
matches2 = re.findall(r'timezone|timezone|tzinfo|tz_offset', content[:800])
print("timezone matches:", matches2)
